concepts.learning_objective: Identify description, prediction, explanation, control and application as the goals of psychological enquiry.
Distinguish between prediction, explanation and control of behaviour with examples.

topics.title: Steps in scientific research and alternative paradigms
topics.ncert_sections: Steps in Conducting Scientific Research; Alternative Paradigms of Research

concepts.learning_objective: Sequence the four steps of scientific research and explain the role of a hypothesis.
Contrast the scientific and interpretive traditions of psychological research.
Explain why psychological data are tied to context, method and theory.
Classify information as demographic, physical, physiological or psychological data.
Describe selection, recording and analysis in scientific observation and the risk of observer bias.
Distinguish naturalistic from controlled and participant from non-participant observation.

topics.title: Experimental method
topics.ncert_sections: Experimental Method; Box 2.1; Field Experiments and Quasi Experiments

concepts.learning_objective: Identify independent, dependent and extraneous variables in an experiment.
Explain experimental and control groups and techniques such as elimination, matching, counter-balancing and random assignment.
Distinguish laboratory, field and quasi experiments and evaluate their strengths and limits.
Interpret positive, negative and zero correlation coefficients ranging from +1.0 to -1.0.
Compare interviews, questionnaires and telephone surveys and state the strengths and limits of surveys.

topics.title: Psychological testing and case study
topics.ncert_sections: Psychological Testing; Types of Tests; Case Study

concepts.learning_objective: Explain objectivity, reliability, validity and norms of a standardised test.
Classify tests as verbal, non-verbal or performance, individual or group, and speed or power.
Describe the case study method, its uses and its limitations.

topics.title: Analysis of data, limitations and ethical issues
topics.ncert_sections: Analysis of Data; Limitations of Psychological Enquiry; Ethical Issues

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish quantitative from qualitative analysis of data.
Explain the lack of a true zero point, relative nature of tools and subjective interpretation as limitations.
Apply the ethical principles of voluntary participation, informed consent, debriefing, sharing results and confidentiality.
